# MCP durable deployment admission

This source packet addresses the MCP and CLI portion of PROD-DUR-01/02/03/04/08, PROD-UX-02 and PROD-PKG-05. The full 78 production criteria remain unchanged. The author has not run a compiler, tests, services, database, Temporal, browser, API or cloud verification, and has made no commit or acceptance decision.

The former adapter called raw Temporal starts, claimed with an MCP holder incompatible with worker custody, and invented a deployment ID without a product row. The new adapter calls the existing canonical `startWorkflowIntent` for deploy and day-two work. A confirmed initial claim uses `workflow:<operationId>` and a five-minute lease. A running retry or competing claim requires a retained native start intent. The canonical intent retains one permanent attempt, strict original-history readback and nonreplayable uncertain state. MCP does not reset that state or send a second transport attempt. A terminal ledger reply carries status only and does not imply a confirmed workflow.

Deploy preparation reserves a deterministic product deployment using tenant, human, integration, capability and key identity. It reads a fresh tenant graph and an uncached, workspace-bound revision manifest, verifies the existing linked/verified execution route, and captures complete manifest JSON, graph, environment, connection, revision, build, message and estimate semantics. Canonical request size, schema and secret guards run before product mutation. A native current-policy check refuses denied preparation before creating a reservation. The product commit completes before broker proposal. The exact native operation is then associated and committed before ACK. Existing reservations and associations are compared, never forced or overwritten. A changed request with the same key refuses.

The two stores do not share a transaction. A pre-proposal crash can leave an unbound workflow projection. A lost projection or broker ACK is recovered with the exact original key and semantics. A lost association ACK can recover only that same association. Optimistic product version conflicts refuse. A claim lost before the native intent exists cannot be reconstructed by MCP. The projection does not consume approval, provide native execution authority or settle a provider outcome.

Execution requires the exact proposing integration and human, current grant scope, exact proposal digest and native approved status. It validates the committed product association and current uncached source semantics before claiming, and repeats a fresh validation after the awaited claim immediately before calling canonical start admission. Existing OAuth authentication, strict tool schemas, browser-only approval and exact proposal/plan digest checks remain mandatory. Approval links now point to `/platform/operations/<id>`. Native approval round metadata is returned only when supplied by the broker detail.

The trusted current integration directory replaces the former generic fallback after a denied role. Native credentials are minted as `cred_<UUID>` by both credential authorities; OAuth grants are minted as `integration_<UUID>` by browser consent. The directory reads current native inventory first, retains revoked/expired refusal, rejects collisions or duplicates and never asks OAuth for a native or unknown namespace. OAuth requires one persisted grant under the current configured issuer and an independently matching subject/client/workspace key read. Unknown, missing, malformed, foreign, expired, revoked, ambiguous or unavailable replies refuse. Caller labels, copied scopes and metadata do not select authority. Existing fresh human membership, deadline, signal and role cap remain in force; the directory read follows the awaited membership read. Journal startup or OAuth configuration unavailability fails closed.

## Revision 2 native final admission

Revision 1 remains frozen under its original receipt. Revision 2 changes only the nine declared paths. Its opener and index delta starts from the exact independently reviewed AWS opener postimages and is frozen separately so integration preserves that dependency. The product projection and proposal remain separate commits. Revision 2 closes the product and source mutation window inside canonical MCP start admission for the verified co-resident default topology described below.

The canonical repository derives its capture from the owning, locked native operation. It reads the public project, environment, revision, revision manifest, deployment and connection using that same database, validates their tenant and immutable association, and recomputes the complete manifest, expanded graph, environment and connection semantics against the retained native proposal. MCP workflow arguments must bind its exact owning connection and `preApproved: true`. The capture includes native provider verification, all current workspace GitHub binding rows or their true absence, every immutable source row for the operation, its full service and pipeline recipes, and the original non-simulated source review evidence. The current transaction retains only approval-relevant project, revision, deployment and environment fields. Working copies, display names, history labels, progress and newer UI pointers can advance while the exact approved revision remains authoritative. Raw saved manifest, connection/configuration, source, full recipe, binding and evidence JSON remain exact.

The capture also reads the integration subject directly from the locked operation and requires one current co-resident `public.members` row with exact `{id, workspace_id, role}` and an editor or admin role. Capture precedes the awaited current role and policy reads. The final statement repeats that native membership identity and role, so a demotion, removal or workspace move committed during the later grant lookup refuses even if that lookup returns the earlier role. Email, display metadata and member version changes alone preserve admission. The final prepared-intent insert, prepared-intent revalidation and permanent attempt CAS repeat the exact native product/source predicates in a fresh READ COMMITTED statement after those awaits. A committed replacement, removal, foreign tenant, raw JSON mutation or source binding revocation refuses before start transport. Existing operation, lease, policy and exact approval predicates stay mandatory. No public product, source, resource or GitHub binding row is locked across the remote role reads. Source sets and native aggregates use matching ASCII lexical order. Captures above two megabytes, or source and planning evidence sets above 10,000 rows, refuse; these are fail-closed availability bounds.

New MCP writes also require a genuine, live opener-created PostgreSQL handle and the actual cached default Supabase client. Private factory registration exposes only a read-only scalar target predicate. It captures the native SDK method/prototype identity, default REST endpoint and public schema, rejects unknown or changed clients without evaluating method accessors, and returns no keys, headers or client options. Existing client construction and caching behavior is preserved. This establishes configured construction provenance, not API authentication or effective permissions.

Supported final MCP admission requires `ZENITH_STORE=postgres`, an unmodified default client built from the module-captured HTTPS `<project-ref>.supabase.co` endpoint, and identical configured product/platform SQL host, database, user and connection options. The SQL endpoint must identify that same hosted project through `db.<project-ref>.supabase.co` with user `postgres`, or the standard Supavisor pooler with user `postgres.<project-ref>`, with an explicit URL port of 5432 or 6543. The opener privately captures the immutable actual opening host, port, database and username, including the pooler realm, before the awaited driver boundary. Missing URL ports cannot acquire new MCP target provenance because the driver may read a changed `PGPORT` after that await. Existing general opener behavior is unchanged; older cached handles without target provenance refuse new MCP writes until reopened. The native session must read database `postgres`, role `postgres`, schema `public`. These endpoint forms follow the current [Supabase connection documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres). Passwords and service keys are neither compared nor returned. Custom API domains, custom SQL roles or schemas, self-hosted endpoints, separate product stores, unavailable configuration, foreign endpoints and arbitrary copied public rows fail closed for new MCP start writes. They are not claimed as supported MCP dispatch topologies by this packet. Root must verify actual hosted composition and role provenance before release.

Prepared retries recapture current owning semantics and preserve the original intent binding. Attempted and acknowledged intents are read before the new topology check, so repository-level recovery after a restart or source/configuration drift remains evidence only with `dispatch: false`. The current public MCP execute tool still performs fresh product validation before reaching this repository: unavailable or changed public semantics can block that evidence-only retry. End-to-end tool retry availability is a separate follow-up in `src/lib/agent-access/v3/tools/execute.ts`, outside this nine-path delta. A lost permanent attempt commit acknowledgement supplies no transport proof and never permits another attempt. No process-local capture map, caller proof, authority flag, store selector, default client override or new broker/queue is added. An already accepted transport call cannot be retracted.

## Revision 3 source coverage and final provenance correction

Revision 3 is a separate six-path incremental packet based on the exact revision 2 tree. The original revision 1 and revision 2 receipts, patches and worktree bytes remain unchanged. Independent review rejected revision 2 pending these bounded corrections; this revision makes no author acceptance claim.

When a concrete native plan digest exists, canonical Start capture now requires one retained immutable snapshot for every managed built container service or scheduled job and its exact owning build pipeline. This is the existing supported source set derived by the owning worker. Its complete retained set must match the approved source digest and review display. Deleting both all retained rows and every source marker no longer turns a concrete managed build into source-free admission. Initial planning with a null native plan digest and genuine source/review absence remains permitted. The new independent-pool controls test combined absence before both prepare and claim, with unchanged native proposal/input/plan digests; direct capture refusal prevents a later approval failure from masking the defect. Existing source-free, individual source faults, source binding, recipe and nonreplay controls remain.

Canonical prepare, prepared revalidation and claim now repeat genuine default opening and cached SDK provenance after the awaited roles and policy checks. The session identity query uses the current owning transaction, never the original occupied single-connection pool. Current composition is checked again after that query so configuration or nested SDK drift during the query also refuses. No caller proof, hook, registration, authority flag or alternate production store is added. The recognized isolated broker seam retains its explicit hosted-composition omission.

The locked postgres.js 3.4.7 parser forwards unknown URL query keys into its startup message. That message can override its URL user or database, including a shared pooler realm. New immutable target provenance now accepts only no query options or one `sslmode=require` or `sslmode=verify-full`. Unknown startup settings, user/database overrides, other TLS modes and duplicate options refuse that proof. General legacy driver construction remains unchanged. This is a compatibility restriction for new MCP writes, and the TLS constructor control does not claim a completed TLS handshake. Actual native PostgreSQL controls open deliberately different URL user/database labels with query overrides, show the server's real original identity, and verify that the private target predicate refuses both labels. A hosted pooler is not contacted.

The actual default SDK factory now privately retains its REST object and own descriptors, REST prototype, native `from` and `schema` methods, and original fetch function and descriptor. Nested substitutions, accessors, copied REST objects and descriptor drift refuse provenance. The predicate reads no keys, headers or options and does not evaluate substituted accessors. Exact restoration retains cached-client behavior. Older cached factory registrations without this complete identity refuse new MCP writes until reconstructed; their ordinary SDK behavior remains unchanged.

Held-role native-CAS controls exercise current opening/configuration and actual nested SDK predicates with explicitly modeled hosted endpoint association, human/grant directory and policy replies. Their initial and final composition checks are protocol models around the genuine private target and SDK predicates, and the final session query runs on actual PostgreSQL. They prove canonical post-role wiring and permanent attempt refusal, not actual default hosted composition. The dedicated SDK controls instantiate the locked client and test nested substitutions and original restoration without network calls. All new controls are unrun by the author. Actual hosted composition, current OAuth/journal authority, genuine Temporal history and later provider APPLY acceptance remain root-owned follow-ups.

## Revision 4 immutable-source fixture correction

Independent review found that revision 3's two combined-absence controls tried to delete authentically retained source rows. Canonical schema13 rejects that mutation before admission. Revision 3 remains frozen with its correction-required receipts. This separate two-path fixture packet changes the source-authority test and this handoff only. Production source, immutable triggers, every existing 72 PostgreSQL and 17 SDK identity, all original revision 2 callback bodies and the legitimate null-plan positive remain unchanged.

The corrected controls begin with an authentic managed Git operation whose source has never been retained. Direct native capture first permits its legitimate null-plan state. An independent PostgreSQL pool then commits an explicitly corrupt concrete normalized planning fixture that omits source retention and every source review marker from creation. Direct capture now must refuse the omission before an approval or intent binding check can mask the guard. Each negative admission preserves the committed proposal, input and concrete plan digests, leaves no permanent attempt, and calls no modeled transport start. There is no retained-row deletion or trigger waiver.

The claim branch honestly prepares the legitimate initial null-plan intent before the corrupt concrete plan is committed. Its request binding remains exact and is asserted unchanged. The corrupt concrete plan also affects the later approval prerequisites, which can independently refuse admission. That claim result is a no-attempt control; it is not isolated proof of a claim-only omission guard. The direct native capture comparison establishes the concrete coverage refusal. Planning documents and transport counters remain explicit models, with no real Temporal transport, saved OpenTofu binary, hosted directory or cloud call. All author compiler, lint, PostgreSQL, SDK and runtime checks remain unrun; root owns execution and independent acceptance.

## Evidence scope and remaining work

The revision 1 PostgreSQL suite still uses the actual owning platform broker and native intent store, independently readable SQL projection commits, version conflicts and permanent attempts. Its product PostgREST and readiness replies remain explicit protocol models. Revision 2 adds the exact committed public collection DDL and native rows as final admission prerequisites, using the promoted-column/data split defined by the current product adapters. All original 18 case bodies and assertions remain unchanged. Private REST-model schemas are dropped after each case; unique native platform/product fixture rows and their tombstones live only for the root-owned database lifetime.

The new final-admission suite uses actual owning PostgreSQL brokers, immutable source capture/retention and planning evidence, independent mutation and claimant pools, and held current-role replies. The subject membership controls read actual native membership, then hold an explicitly valid modeled grant reply while an independent pool commits member changes; the stale editor reply still returns, making the final native predicate the refusal boundary. They also preserve unchanged membership and benign member metadata. GitHub HTTP, the current human/integration directory and transport counters are explicit models. The corrupt foreign-source fixture is labeled and checked directly by native source capture before later approval refusal can hide it. Normalized planning documents are synthetic SQL review fixtures, not saved OpenTofu binaries. The isolated start store is the existing recognized test-only broker seam; it omits the hosted endpoint check while retaining the real native product/source statements. The SDK protocol cases instantiate the locked native client without a network call and use generated, unlogged ephemeral constructor material. Neither suite proves actual default Supabase topology, live product REST/OAuth, effective provider permissions or genuine Temporal history readback. The agent journal grant store remains a distinct authority. This packet does not claim atomic authorization or revocation across the product database and that separate store.

The later saved-plan provider dispatch has a separate current target gap. `src/lib/execution/apply.ts` reads public environment connection/region before the paired runtime awaits roles in `src/lib/platform/plan-artifacts.ts`. The current native capture and CAS in `src/lib/controlplane/db/repos/plan-artifacts.ts` fence native source, recipes and GitHub binding, but do not yet predicate that public owning target. An authorized public environment connection replacement/removal, foreign scope or region change during those awaits can retain the original plan bytes while changing current target authority. Closing MCP start admission does not close that later provider dispatch boundary. Root assigned it a separate source packet; these paths are unchanged here. The internal owning native capture/final predicate contract can inform that follow-up, with its own topology and original-byte authority review.

Root must verify the default current directory against the actual canonical agent journal and product REST authority, with consistent trusted worker configuration, then run the existing actual Temporal canonical lane and an MCP deploy handoff using genuine retained original history. Browser/API/CLI integration, current provider-target custody and provider outcome projection remain separately authorized runtime checks. All authored revision 2 and revision 3 cases are unrun. The complete DUR/G2 and full 78 production criteria remain open. No migration, queue, default server, broker guard relaxation or production environment bypass was added.

Canonical gate registration is outside ownership. Revision 1 `CASE-CONTRACT.json` lists its 24 additional required PostgreSQL names and seven existing Temporal controls that must remain required. Revision 2 and revision 3 `CASE-CONTRACT.json` receipts list the exact additional final-admission PostgreSQL identities under `ZENITH_TEST_MCP_START_SOURCE_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED=1`, plus SDK protocol identities separately. Keep `ZENITH_TEST_MCP_DEPLOY_ADMISSION_REQUIRED=1` and `ZENITH_TEST_DEFAULT_CURRENT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED=1`. Use an explicitly owned PostgreSQL URL and canonical schema13. Required flags without PostgreSQL throw before the suite can skip. No PGlite replacement, skip waiver or gate edit is included in this packet.
